utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday, by the end of the day we were speaking about the various different -- other Red Beret camps that you got information about. And just briefly, was there a camp called Bilje near Osijek in Eastern Slavonia, and who was in charge there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, the last information I have was that the commander was Vlasto Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And before him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before him, Zika Crnogorac.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And was there a camp Knezevi Vinogradi near Beli Menastir in Eastern Slavonia? And who was in command there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, to the best of my knowledge, according to what a man told me at the Bistrica Hotel in Jahorina, so according to his story there was a camp in Knezevi Vinogradi and in Bilje, and he said to me that Vaso Mijovic was practically in charge of all of Baranja.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the Pajzos camp near Bapska, did you actually see that camp at some point in time? And do you know who the commander was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that Zvjezdan Jovanovic was commander of the camp. I was never in the camp though. I know that Pajzos camp is near Bapska. I know that from the time I was in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And finally, the Tikves camp. What can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for what I know about the Tikves camp, this is really based on what Pero Divljak told me. He said to me that they had come from that camp when they came to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let's turn -- return to the camp in Boracko Jezero. Was there a time that the Red Berets and the recruits were transferred to a location close to Mostar to enforce the Herzegovina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And where were you taken and were there any other troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, after about a month that I spent in that camp - I don't know at whose request this was - but the local Serb forces or rather, the Herzegovina Brigade had major problems in the region of Podvelezje. I was never there before. I thought that Podvelezje was one village, but there are actually ten villages there. In one of these village, they met with resistance. They could not break through, so they put in a request. I don't know how this happened. They asked for reinforcements. And that's why they transferred us to Podvelezje.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, when you look back at the map that you were given in the beginning, you see this -- it's a region between Nevesinje and Mostar, right -- on the right side from Mostar. There's a whole region with that name that we just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: While you were there, did you -- did a politician come to visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Vojislav Seselj, accompanied by Zika Crnogorac.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what did the two -- what did they two do in that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What they really wanted is something that I actually don't know. However, the two of them did come together. It was the first time I saw Seselj. It was the first time I saw Zika Crnogorac too. Seselj brought cigarettes for his volunteers. And immediately everybody gathered around him. Whereas, Zika talked to Aco Legija.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So the Seselj volunteers were also at that location and involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Seselj's volunteers too, and the men from Vukovar, the Vukovarci, and these forces of the newly established Herzegovina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would need to go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The headquarters of the White Wolves, where were they located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Jahorina, in the forest-keeper's small house.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, when you look at the map, there is the -- the whole region Jahorina indicated, and there is an "A," you see the letter "A," that's where the camp was. The witness has marked this map accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the White Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the White Wolves was the late Srdjan Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he a professional soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was he, and what kind of a person was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srdjan Knezevic was a local Serb from Pale. Before the war, he had a coffee bar in Pale. Out of all these men I saw in these areas while I was in Herzegovina and in Sarajevo, Srdjan Knezevic is the only one for whom I can say that he was an honest man up to a degree. I mean, there is no doubt about that, but he was a man who had a unit where there was some kind of discipline.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The unit, was it -- was it integrated in the VRS structure? And if so, in which corps? To which corps did it belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It belonged to the Army of Republika Srpska. Officially it belonged to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. However, General Milosevic did not have any influence whatsoever over Srdjan Knezevic directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who had the influence over Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that on the basis of a million examples. For example, many times Han Pijesak was contacted when Srdjan needed something, and every action that Srdjan undertook was based on contacts with Mladic before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned Han Pijesak. Was that where Mladic was usually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ever hear or see Knezevic refuse to fulfil an order from General Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many times.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in such a case, what would happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing would happen. Absolutely nothing. It would be the way Srdjan said.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The soldiers in the White Wolf unit, what kind of soldiers were they? Where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were all kinds of people there. There were local Serbs from Pale. There were Russians. There were Bulgarians. Seven languages were spoken in the dorm. Most of these people had come from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what uniform did they wear? And did they have a particular patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The uniforms were camouflage uniforms of the Army of Republika Srpska. There were no patches whatsoever on the uniforms because these were Srdjan's explicit orders that nobody should have any kind of patch or insignia on them. The White Wolves never had any kind of patch or insignia on except for the head of a white wolf on their vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that you were stationed in a building, a wood building, at Jahorina. And you have actually prepared a sketch with the help of the investigators. And it's tab 7. It is -- and I have a few questions in relation to the buildings that you have indicated in this sketch. First of all, you have a building with the name "Mladic" in it. What kind of a building was it and why is "Mladic" marked here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Mladic" here because that's what everybody called it in the vernacular. This was a hotel where Mladic had most of his meetings. I don't know how many times we saw his vehicles and his high-ranking officers who had meetings with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you have also indicated this White Wolves's headquarters. And did you actually -- the White Wolves, did you actually sleep in that building when you were in Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the headquarters of the White Wolves, and this is the dormitory for the White Wolves, for people who came from elsewhere. But I don't know whether I was there 20 times in total in this house, and everybody else for that matter. Because we spent most of our time in Trnovo and Treskavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For what reasons did you go to this headquarters in Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would happen only when we would have time off. However, that happened so seldom that I can count it on the fingers of one hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you have indicated also a place, Kosuta, and you put there the name Goran Saric. What kind of a place was Kosuta and who was that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosuta had been a hotel before the war. And when I came there, it was the base of the special police brigade that was commanded by Goran Saric. Its commander was Goran Saric.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you say "special police brigade," of the Republika Srpska? Is that ...?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you have also here the Hotel Bistrica. Who would use that hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hotel Bistrica is also at Jahorina. It was used by the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see government members there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What would they do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them had rooms where they slept. Most of them came there to gorge on food and drink.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the White Wolves also use that -- the kitchen of the hotel to eat and spend time there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every time they would have time off, or rather, when we would have time off, Srdjan's orders were that they had to give us food there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Srdjan Knezevic ever asked to join the police forces with this unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what was his reaction to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when these two monkeys from the MUP came, they came with a briefcase full of money, and they made this offer to Srdjan. They said that there was no need for him to go into action, no need to do anything. He was just supposed to provide security for Karadzic. At the end of this story, there were four or five of us there, and we tried to save these two men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but we can't use expressions like "monkeys." It doesn't assist. Who are we talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You heard that. About whom are we talking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are men from the MUP, from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you know their names or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Srdjan knew them personally. They were some local men from Pale. I had never seen them in my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And why did Srdjan -- how did he react to the offer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, we tried to save those two from being killed by him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So he rejected it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that you usually were in -- on other location, and you mentioned Treskavica and Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is indicated on the map again, the region. It's an entire region. And indicated is here with letter "B." It's indicated here with the letter "B." And Trnovo is actually right above -- let's say 2 centimetres above the letter "B."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, when you were in Trnovo, where would the White Wolf unit stay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the school building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Which other units did you see in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were members of the police there, of the police of Republika Srpska, mostly from Kula. Also, there was a police station from Trnovo. There were members of the Army of Republika Srpska from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Their commander was Cedo Sladoje.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were any Seselj Chetniks there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the major offensive of the Muslim forces, there was Slavko Aleksic from Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when was that major offensive?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have mentioned just this person, Aleksic, Slavko Aleksic from -- no, I'll come to him a little bit later. In the school in Trnovo, were there only Serb soldiers housed or also Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A platoon, a work platoon, from Doboj was accommodated there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Where did they -- did they directly come from Doboj, or were they from some other place, transferred from a different place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know I know from what they said, that is, that they were from Doboj. However, as far as I know, they were first transferred to the prison at Kula in Sarajevo and from there they were transferred to Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Does that mean they were detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And why were -- what were they used for in Trnovo? Why were they there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, they called them a labour platoon and they were used to dig trenches and dugouts along the frontlines at Treskavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the White Wolves order them to do such things, or who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was their superior. They just slept there in the same building. The White Wolves and Srdjan Knezevic couldn't give them any orders because the White Wolves never held the lines, the frontlines.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In early May 1995, did the White Wolves participate in a combat operation in Debelo Brdo, above the cemetery -- the Jewish cemetery in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was the task given to the White Wolves and who gave them this task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, a letter came from the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, signed by General Milosevic, to the effect that Ratko Mladic had given orders to Srdjan Knezevic to make a breakthrough at Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And -- yes. Can you continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Srdjan in those days could not get in touch with Mladic because Mladic was already somewhere around Bihac, I think; anyway, at the other end of Republika Srpska. And there was a major dispute between Srdjan and his deputy, Cvjetko Gacanin, because Srdjan wasn't willing to undertake this operation on Debelo Brdo because it was very heavily fortified. However, as he didn't wish to go against Mladic's order, the decision was taken to carry out that operation after all.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who -- which other unit was involved in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko Aleksic's Chetniks, acting from the direction of the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you meet this person, this Chetnik, and what can you tell us about his activities in the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see Slavko Aleksic, because often with Srdjan or some other persons - I can't remember where - we went together to Grbavica. As for any other units, I never heard that anyone hadn't committed any crimes in Sarajevo or anything like that. I only heard this about Slavko Aleksic and his men from Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he constantly in the region of Grbavica, and what was his task there, his general task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Slavko Aleksic was in Grbavica from the beginning of the war and he held the line at the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have now displayed on the -- on the Sanction system a picture. Was that picture shown to you in -- it's tab 10 in the binder, but it's actually an exhibit already used, Your Honours. It's Exhibit 451, tab 24. Was this photo shown to you, and did you recognise the person, despite the quality -- the bad quality of the photo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's from the Exhibit 458.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Slavko Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: During the operation at Debelo Brdo, did the White Wolves have heavy losses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was the -- was Knezevic himself wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you present when -- did General Mladic appear at some point in time at Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to refer to the beginning of the story, because as I was saying, Srdjan couldn't contact Mladic, and this operation was under preparation for some seven days, a little more or less. I can't remember exactly. However, when it started, we suffered very great losses within a span of five minutes, and upon withdrawing - now, I can't remember whether we first went to the hospital with Srdjan and came back and then met Mladic or whether this was immediately after we had pulled out - but Mladic appeared suddenly, unexpectedly, and I just happened to be there by chance because I was helping Srdjan because he couldn't walk. And when Mladic appeared, Milosevic was there all the time, coming and going. The first sentence uttered by Mladic was, "Who told you to go to the president without my permission?" And I found this very strange, because up until then I hadn't heard that anyone went to the president, nor that he needed permission. Then he slapped him a couple of times, tore off his rank insignia, and that is all I saw, because Srdjan just made a sign to me, indicating that I should move away, I should get lost.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can I just make a clarification for the record, please. It's Prosecution's Exhibit 458, tab 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: To clarify who slapped whom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mladic slapped Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you subsequently find out whether Mladic actually had ordered this attack on Debelo Brdo or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we all found that out later on from Srdjan. Mladic hadn't ordered that attack, and that was the reason why he slapped Milosevic, because this had been done arbitrarily, or rather, in agreement with Karadzic. Milosevic had used the White Wolves to capture Debelo Brdo, thinking that the operation would succeed, so that Karadzic to say to Mladic that he'd been around Sarajevo for three years and Milosevic had managed to capture Debelo Brdo. So this was an attempt to remove Mladic from the leadership of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you get this information from Knezevic, or how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly from Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: After the activity in Debelo Brdo, did you take part in this major operation in Treskavica, when the Muslim offensive took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Which Serb troops were involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, when the Muslim forces launched the offensive, the only people remaining in Trnovo were the White Wolves. All the others had scattered. And then the Wolves from Drina, Marko Pavlovic, Legenda's [phoen] Wolves arrived to help. And during this first attack, the Wolves suffered considerable losses. And after that, upon Mladic's orders, we were dispatched to Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you were in Jahorina, did you see any troops arriving from outside the area? And if so, which troops did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I first saw in Kasindol Ljubo Mauzer's Panthers and when we arrived at Jahorina and went to the Bistrica Hotel, on the way to the Hotel Bistrica, in front of the Kosuta Hotel, we first saw vehicles with license plates of the Republic of Srpska Krajina. And after that, people in black uniforms with markings of Arkan's Tigers and others with Skorpije markings and people from the MUP of Srpska Krajina. Some of them were in black uniforms and others in the standard police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was in charge of these troops coming from the Krajina and the Tigers? Could you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vaso Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see him at Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And had you seen him before in the Buna camp or in Jezero camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Vaso Mijovic on one occasion at the camp at Boracka Jezero. But what I was surprised by, because when I saw him at that time he was a driver, and the young man that I spoke to at the Bistrica Hotel on Jahorina, he said that Vaso Mijovic was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned the person Mauzer. Do you know what his correct name was and where did he come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, his name is Ljubisa Savic. His nickname is Mauzer, and he's from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers with scorpion patches as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, I had no idea, because that was the first time for me to see people with such insignia, and it was the first time I had heard of the name Scorpions. But later on, staying in Vukovar, I learnt that it was a unit from that area whose commander was a certain Boco.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to show you now just a few patches. And this -- this is here Exhibit 349, tab 5. What -- what patch is that? Which -- what is written on the patch and which unit wore it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the special guards, the Panthers. They were Ljubo Mauzer's panthers from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And then Exhibit 349, tab 4. What kind of a patch is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arkan's Tigers.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And now I would like to put to you tab 8 of the witness Exhibit 460. It is a note dated the 24th of July, 1995 from the commander of the IKM [phoen] Staff Savo Cvjetinovic. And it refers to the situation at the Trnovo battlefront. First of all, do you know this person Savo Cvjetinovic and what position he had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that man. I've never even heard of him in my whole life.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At that time you see here 24th of July, 1995. Were you still at the frontline in Treskavica and Trnovo, or had you already left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And reference in this document is made to the Scorpions unit of the Serbian MUP. Do you -- were you aware that the Scorpions were a police unit related to the Serbian MUP, or is that not known to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And reference is made here -- there is a sentence saying: "During the day, we will organise part of the company from Trebinje to go to Nevesinje and attend Commander Zirgjevic's funeral, Dragan Zirojevic was deputy commander to the late Nebojisa Sukic." Do you know this person Zirojevic? Who was he? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Dragan Zirojevic. He's from Nevesinje. He was also one of the first 57 Red Berets. Dragan Zirojevic came together with all of the Red Berets to Mostar. And after the Red Berets, that is, those from Serbia had gone to Serbia, he became the commander or chief of the police station in Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And were you aware that he got killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was killed in -- on Treskavica or any other combat action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Zirojevic was killed at Treskavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That should be enough for this. While you were still in the region of Sarajevo and Treskavica, did international forces start bombing Pale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you recall the time of the year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that it was immediately after the operation on Debelo Brdo, because we attended the funeral of White Wolves members when the bombing started.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you get information in relation to activities of a certain Nikola Ribic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nikola Ribic, also known as Kanada, was a member of the White Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did he do in relation to the bombing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikola Ribic, on his own initiative, without receiving orders from anyone, captured two members of UNPROFOR or observers, whatever they were, took their jeep, and tied them to a mast at Pale -- to a bridge at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you present when Knezevic got a -- a call on the Motorola related to that issue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What -- can you explain what you heard and what the circumstances were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Kanada had done what he did, I think that we were at the Sandro coffee bar and he came there. And shortly after him Knezevic arrived. Kanada told him what he had done. And quickly after that a call came over the Motorola and the White Wolf was being looked -- asked for by Vihor. I can't remember whether it was Vihor I or II, but it was Vihor. I am 100 per cent sure of that. And Srdjan was given permission for the operation to continue, that he had done well and that he should continue with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What were the exact words? Do you recall the words that you heard this Vihor I or II say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly what the words were, but what I can remember is that it was in connection with what Kanada had done, that it was a good thing, and that the operation should be continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Vihor I or II, did you know who used that caller ID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. Vihor I or II - I'm not sure which - is the code name for Momcilo Krajisnik, or rather, his office.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the preparations for the operation against Debelo Brdo, just by chance - because code names are changed frequently - Srdjan for the crew of recoilless gun used the code name Vihor, upon which a man from the security unit of Radovan Karadzic came to Srdjan to tell him personally that that code name could not be used because it was Momcilo Krajisnik's code name. And we also received information of the same contents from the communications centre at Jahorina, of which the code name is Labud III.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And after this conversation on the Motorola that you heard, were more hostages taken and were the White Wolves involved in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was personally present, close to the hotel - I think its name was Panorama - and a house was there in which the observers or UNPROFOR were put up. And Srdjan was also there. And it was explicitly ordered that all the military equipment should be collected and that personal belongings could not be taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I forgot to ask you: You mentioned that you were in a place like Sandro cafe or bar. Where is that? Where is it located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sandro coffee bar is at Pale, and its owner was a man who worked in a unit of Srdjan Knezevic. He was in the logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you know how this whole hostage-taking affair ended? Did you get information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was saying, I was present when that house was being searched and when the hostages were taken from there, the operation acquired broad proportions, so that at Grbavica Slavko Aleksic's Chetniks had a conflict with the French Foreign Legion, also the military barracks at Lukavica. And towards the end of the day, together with Knezevic and I think a couple of others from the White Wolves, we went to the Lukavica headquarters where Knezevic went to attend a meeting with General Milosevic. Because you can't go inside, I went to the building of the military police to see their commander Cvoro, who told me that Jovica Stanisic and the Red Berets from Serbia were involved in this operation regarding the hostages and their equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: While you were in the wider Sarajevo region in the years 1994 and 1995, did you observe deliveries of weapons coming from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many times, especially in front of the building of the military police. There were civilian trucks with license plates from Serbia. I personally never got into the truck to see what was inside, but from people who were members of that unit I learnt that there were new rifles or ammunition or whatever it was they were delivering.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You say "in front of the building of the military police." Can you be more specific? What kind of a building are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the building in which the military police was housed of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Their commander was Captain Cvoro. And they used the military police building and the trucks always entered at night, because at the other gate there were UNPROFOR members or, rather, members of the French Foreign Legion who controlled everything coming in and going out from the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see these kind of trucks also in Pale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many times in front of the police building at Pale, or in the area where the warehouses are, where the timber mill is at Pale. On many occasions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: While you were in combat actions, did you happen to notice where the ammunition you used came from and when it was produced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Many times I would say, for instance, PPU, which meant Prvi Partizan Uzice and the year of production, now, whether it was 1993 or 1994 -- but anyway, it was one of the years of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: After the NATO bombing, you said you were in Harli [phoen]: Did you come across a partly blown-up storage facility, and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was when we went to see Sljivo, who was a security man in the White Wolves, and his house is right next to the warehouse of the Army of Republika Srpska. As during the shelling the -- half of the warehouse no longer existed, and that was the first time that I saw rockets which they call Krmace or sows.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you describe these rockets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say -- that is all I can say about them, because I saw them from a distance, and this was something enormous. And it wasn't in boxes but it was on some kind of stands. And I never in my life saw such a rocket being launched, nor did I ever see the effects of such a rocket. That was the first and last time I saw them in my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we need to go now into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I begin my cross-examination of this witness, I should like to draw your attention one and all to the fact that these secret witnesses are being significantly abused in order to place information which is wholly untrue and incorrect. And I'm going to prove that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Your job at the moment is to ask questions of the witness, not make observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Private session. This was all --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why, Mr. May?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. C-017. You spoke here about the events in Mostar and the surrounding parts at that material time, the time you testified about. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that the events in Mostar from those times are well known to you; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, I'm going to ask you a few questions to which you can give me brief answers. You can say whether you know about it or don't know about it. Do you know that at the end of the summer of 1991, that is to say, the time you mentioned yourself, this period, in Mostar the Patriotic League, a paramilitary Muslim formation, was formed? Did you hear anything about that? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say on the subject is this: I knew that there was a strong stronghold of the SDA. As far as the Patriotic League is concerned, that was the only time -- the only time I saw it or heard about it was on BH television, whether before the war or a little after the war had started in Sarajevo. That's as far as I know about the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. When you say there was a strong stronghold of the SDA in Mostar, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean that at that particular time, most of the inhabitants of Mostar were Muslim by ethnicity and that they had a very strong party there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And do you remember some other events? Because at that particular time, as far as I understood it, you were there in the area throughout. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you remember the attack launched by the Muslim forces on Djuro Salaj on the Buna on the 1st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that, because at that particular time I was in Mostar, which means during April. Whether it was the end of March or the beginning of April, I can't quite remember, but I ended up being in prison in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And do you know that from the motel called the Buna Motel, the Muslim extremists started shooting at a military vehicle? Do you happen to remember that particular event and that the JNA members arrested five reserve policemen? They released them the same day, by the way. But there was shooting at the members of the Yugoslav army in those days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, yes, there were incidents, sporadic gunfire or whatever you like to call them, between the reserve or active composition of the JNA, and these local police forces. Under whose command they were, I really can't say. But as I've already said, I was in a cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, do you know about the terrorist attack on the JNA barracks called Severni Logor, Northern Camp, at the beginning of April? Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. If we're thinking of the same thing, if we're thinking about the truck where some explosive devices were planted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am thinking about that cistern truck that caused an explosion and the explosion could be heard far wider than Mostar. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That took place on the 3rd of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't say. I'm not very good with dates. I can't remember. It was in April, yes, it was. Now, what the exact day was, I don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you remember that 30 civilians were wounded and that one soldier was killed following that incident and that four were seriously wounded and three men less seriously wounded? Do you remember that? I assume you do because it was an event that everybody knew about in Mostar. Mostar isn't a big town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the fact that a certain number of people were injured and that considerable material damage was caused to the JNA barracks, I do know that, yes. Because yes, it was a well-known event in Mostar. But once again, as to the figures of who was wounded and killed, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, how did this event and occurrence impact on the citizens of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was fear. And what I can tell you, what I know and can say, is that the Serbs began to leave Mostar in masses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, how many Serbs lived in Mostar before the war, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for me personally, it's a difficult question to answer, because I consider myself to be a Yugoslav, from the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the country I was born in. So I really never asked anybody in my life whether they were a Serb, a Croat, or Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I just asked you. If you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, after that attack, the attack that everybody in Mostar knew about, did you hear about attacks by the HOS and Green Berets on military facilities, especially the military airport, airstrip, and these attacks became frequent later on? On the 9th of April, for example, a soldier was killed and several others were wounded and the armed attacks around the JNA became more and more frequent and gained in intensity during those days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, the events that took place round about, there were rumours going round, but I personally was in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you happen to remember the event that took place when close to Mostar ten soldiers were captured and three superior officers after the truce that was agreed upon in Sarajevo and related to the entire territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which truce are you talking about? Which cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The 13th of April. You don't know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember another event, when some pilots were kidnapped, Major Milan Micic and Captain First Class Dragan Arsovski from the airport in Mostar? Do you remember them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially. It rings a bell. I'm vaguely -- I vaguely remember something like that happening, but I really can't remember the details around the whole event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you know what was going on, for example, on the 26th of April, what happened then, when these formations, the ones we're discussing, attacked the barracks of the Mostar battalion? Do you know where the Mostar Battalion barracks are located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where the northern and southern camps are located, but I don't know the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, you don't know names. But do you remember the attack on the barracks on the 26th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, do you remember this: That on the 27th of April this time in Mostar, we saw the arrival of UNPROFOR forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then there was some provocations, and there was artillery fire coming from both sides, precisely when the UNPROFOR forces arrived. And there are facts and figures about that, information about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, then. Do you know who controlled at the time, apart from the soldiers who were in the barracks there, the JNA soldiers, who was in control of the Mostar region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, the situation was very murky, because I

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, is it quite clear that it was for the most part these paramilitary formations, that is to say, the HOS and the Green Berets or, rather, the Muslim forces, and these paramilitary forces as well, that they controlled the town itself - is that clear - and all the main facilities in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, it was a very murky situation, because the northern camp facility, for example, is in the town itself. The southern camp is towards the exit of the town. And the northern camp was across the road from the Zalik settlement, which means in town, and the army was there. As to the Konak barracks, for example, which before the war was linked to the JNA command or something like that - I really can't say - but you could see military personnel moving about there. That remained under the command, for example, of the Serb forces, or rather, the JNA. Now, between the Konak and the northern camp, that part of town, there was a sort of reserve police force, so the formation that I saw and that took me into custody was officially HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you were arrested and taken into custody by the HOS. Do you know what the HOS is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Croatian Defence Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it is a paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that, yes. I do know that it is a paramilitary formation. At that time it was, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because the HOS was treated as a paramilitary formation even by the Croatian authorities, both in Bosnia and in Croatia too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you know that because it's Paraga [phoen] and his extremists; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was particular fear in Mostar from HOS because they knew that Blaz Kraljevic was commander of the unit. So when I was in prison myself, the way in which I was exchanged, for example, was precisely because of this, because people learnt about it. So the people who helped me, actually, were Croats. But they came to learn that they would be transported to Dretelj. And anybody ended up in Dretelj never left it in one piece. And if he did leave it in one piece, he was a bit deranged. So the people were there from Blaz Kraljevic's unit, that is to say, people from Western Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that when it comes to HOS, the Croatian authorities themselves ordered that HOS had to be subordinated to the Croatian army or disbanded? If they refused to join the Croatian army and become subordinated to it, in Bosnia-Herzegovina that they had to be subservient to the HVO? So they, too, were absolutely astounded by the atrocities that HOS carried out in the region. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as all this is concerned, I stressed in my statement and my testimony that I'm a sportsman myself, so I am apolitical, totally Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. apolitical. And I was there not of my own free will. So all the events around HOS and the military and paramilitary formations, I really can't say anything about that. The only thing I can say is that yes, there was a great deal of fear. Even Croats were afraid. And the young man -- the guy who helped me had a lot of problems with the HOS after I was transferred to Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, this man Blaz Kraljevic and his escorts precisely on the Cule-Mostar road and Croatian territory, they themselves killed because they couldn't come to terms with them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about that story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Because of his self-will, lack of discipline, the atrocities he carried out, and all the rest of it, because everybody suffered from this, both the Serb, Croats, and the Muslims, everybody. It was to their disadvantage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us deal with the witness's evidence, not your comments on it. He can deal with what he knows himself. He can't give evidence -- he can't deal with political matters or what the Croats did. That's for them, and you can give evidence about it if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, as this was the time when you could have known about this - and I told you when UNPROFOR arrived in Mostar - do you remember that on the 3rd of May, in a place between Mostar and Citluk, the representative of the European mission was killed, he was a Belgian, Bertrand Dore [phoen] was his name, and due to that the European mission transferred its offices to Split temporarily because of the security situation there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't remember? All right. Fine. Now, let's move on to the main subject of your testimony. You said that on the 6th of May for St. George's Day, Djurdjevdan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the left bank there was one group, on the right bank there was the JNA and the attack on Mostar. A: Yes Q: And you were very categoric in stating that it was Djurdjevdan, St. George's Day, the 6th of May, the attack.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it was St. George's Day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. 017, there was no attack on Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that right or is that not right? On the 6th of May, there was absolutely no attack on Mostar, none whatsoever, because in the southern camp and in the northern camp was the JNA. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So then how could the JNA come and attack Mostar from somewhere else when it was in Mostar? It withdrew from Mostar on orders later on. So what kind of attack are you talking about? And once they withdrew, there was no attack on Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the JNA withdrew, there was no attack. On the 6th of May, on St. George's Day, on Djurdjevdan, since the area between the southern camp and the northern camp is called the town of Mostar, this is where the attack was carried out, from the right side and from the left side. Or as they called it, the cleansing of Mostar was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What are you talking about? What kind of cleansing of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has given his evidence. He says that was the day. So no real point arguing about it now. But let us adjourn. Twenty minutes. Could you be back, please, Witness C-017 in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, in view of this blockade and the major presence of various paramilitary formations in Mostar, the army could not even move through Mostar; they had to go by helicopter from one barracks to the other or to the positions where they were deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I did hear helicopters many times though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was an order issued by General Perisic, who at that time was garrison commander in Mostar -- or rather, corps commander down there, not to respond to provocations? These provocations were gunfire at military facilities coming from different sides. Do you know anything about this gunfire directed at military facilities and everything else that was going on, and are you aware of this order issued by General Perisic not to respond to provocations, for the army to make an effort to distance itself in every possible way from such conflicts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, you're not aware of that. All right. You were saying that, in addition to the army, there was the Serb Territorial Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Within this Territorial Defence, there were volunteers too; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the Territorial Defence, no. The volunteers, as they called themselves, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that they were not within the Serb Territorial Defence ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because the local Serbs were more afraid of these volunteers than the members of the other local ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to ask you for an explanation now, because you claimed here that there were some Red Berets over there and that they were dominant, as you had put it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that this was a group from Knin or, rather, as you had put it, Knindzas who had been trained by Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My knowledge about that, specifically about that, the Knindzas and the fact that they were trained by Captain Dragan, comes from them themselves. I heard about it from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Various patches were shown to you here, and then you recognised one, saying the police of the Krajina, Milicija Krajina, and other such things. So these were the people who were dominant there. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Later, when you talked about the Boracko Lake, Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff asked you how many of them were there, and you said about ten. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you confirmed that actually all of them but one went there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, how is this possible that about ten of them dominate over there, among all these people who you say were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply, first of all, on the basis of what you were saying and also on the basis of what Seselj's volunteers were saying later, it is well known that all of them, all of them who called themselves volunteers, Seselj's volunteers, or the White Eagles, were trained in Golubic within a 27-day period under the command of these very same Red Berets that were down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where this Golubic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that it was near Knin. I was never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, you were never there. Then explain another thing to me: Since you said yesterday during your testimony that when you got a cap and somebody put it on your head, you didn't even want to take it. Somebody put it on your head. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, since there was a lot of talk about this cap, yes, this man actually put my cap on my head. I did not ask for the cap. And at the time when this was happening, this was not a significant event at all. The fact that he put a cap on my head, because in fact in this formation he was just a little nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just interested in one detail: You say that there was a two-headed eagle on the cap and that on it there was the letters "DB," State Security, Drazavna Bezbednost.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Pero Divljak is the only one who I saw with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Since you are linking this up, although you say that these are people who came from Knin, and you're linking this up with the state security of Serbia, do you know that it is quite impossible for the state security of Serbia to have some kind of a two-headed eagle with the letters saying "State Security" on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about the state security of Serbia in a general context. I can only say what I saw. So as for the state security and Frenki and everything else, I just heard about this from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, you heard about it from them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I did see this sign on the patch. This is what I saw on Pero Divljak's cap. The two-headed eagle with the letters "DB" on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now we're going to get to Pero Divljak too. But was it clear to you then that the two-headed eagle could certainly not be the sign of the state security of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I know that? I have nothing to do with them. The first time I saw these men, I did not know who they were and where they came from and why they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could the legal officer come up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you refer to a large number of persons who you know by name but not in person; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said explicitly in my statement what I saw and what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Apart from this attack that you say took place on the 6th of May -- well, there was no attack, and there weren't any force movements, troop movements. Do you know that the army left on orders? You talked about Perisic's speech to the soldiers. He gave some explanation of his. I'm not going into all of that now. I am not going into that, whether he had information available at the time. But he was probably giving this explanation with the best of intentions, that the army had withdrawn from Mostar actually and that until then the army had been in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was in the southern camp and northern camp, in these barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when the JNA withdrew from Mostar. So we are talking about the period from the 6th of May until the 15th of June. The army completely held under its control the left bank because people talked later on and said that Karadzic had said that Neretva, the Neretva River was a natural boundary, because the paratroopers had taken the other bank one day and then they withdrew the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It has to be the left bank. If it's the eastern bank, because you say which bank is which one if you look at the confluence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me I did not find this quite clear because for me there are no different banks in Mostar. I can't remember who was the first person from whom I heard this, the eastern bank and the western bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, the army could not take Mostar when it was in Mostar in the first place. And once it withdrew from Mostar, afterwards it did not take it any more. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. Now we're talking about the JNA. Before, the army was at the airport, at the Heliodrom. At the Heliodrom actually. Because this is on the right side. That's where a military high school was, called Marsal Tito. And underneath was the Heliodrom. This is Rodoc and Jasenice, those settlements. And before the 6th of May, the army was there, the JNA was there, at the Heliodrom. The army was at the airport, and the other side too, because the aviator's bridge has to be crossed in order to reach the airport. Before entering Mostar, the 63rd Airborne Brigade completely levelled the village of Gnojnice, which is above the airport, with the assistance of reservists from Montenegro. And there were large numbers of them there. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Sarajevo, the army was in the northern camp and in the Konak barracks that was in town. On the right side, that is to say, the neighbourhoods that are on the road to Listica -- or rather, in that direction. They were totally under control. I don't know how to call them, the Croat-Muslim forces. I don't know who commanded them at the time. I really don't know about that particular point in time. However, as for what you're saying, that the army was in Mostar, if the army were in Mostar, I and the rest - I don't know how many of us were in the cell - would not have ended up in prison, because it would have been impossible for me to be in prison arrested by the HOS. And if this same town were held by the Serb forces. This is quite illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is exactly what I wanted to hear from you. When I say "in Mostar," you said just a few minutes ago, you confirmed, that the army was at the airport, at the Heliodrom, at the military high school, and its barracks, the southern camp and the northern camp. So the army was in its own facilities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, until the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the army did not hold Mostar. It was in these military facilities, and the army was being shot at from various quarters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that at that time I was in prison, when there was this sporadic gunfire and all the rest that was going on between these formations and the JNA formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was the Croat and the Muslim forces that held Mostar. That's what you confirmed just now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the army did not carry out an attack against Mostar, and it did not take Mostar. It never took Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true, because the army started an attack on the 6th of May. And as far as I can remember, this attack went on for two days only, because they left the northern camp and the southern camp simultaneously. And I already mentioned all the units that were on that side where I was, on the right side, where the paratroopers were. The composition of the units from the northern camp is something I am not aware of, but I did see people -- these people when the Serb forces, the JNA - call them what you will - when they finally linked up by the Rasvita [phoen] department store. That was the end of this action that they called the cleansing of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How can you talk about the cleansing of Mostar when nobody cleansed Mostar? Mostar was under the control of the Croat and Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. If the JNA forces and the Serb forces, the Territorial Defence and everybody else, enters Mostar, I mean, I don't know. They weren't carrying flowers. As far as I could see, they were carrying lighter weapons or heavier weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. However, they made communication possible. And then the army withdrew from Mostar. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army withdrew on the 15th of June from Mostar. So what I can claim, in relation to this period, and what I saw at the airport, or rather, what I saw at the northern camp barracks, and perhaps two or three days later - I can't remember exactly, because I don't find this important at all - as far as I know, from their stories, it was the Uzice Corps. But I did see the army withdrawing from Nevesinje. That is the only thing I saw concerning the withdrawal of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The army left Mostar. It left its facilities, the facilities where they were. And until then, they held these facilities of theirs. And Mostar was held by the forces that you mentioned. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said, and I underlined awhile ago, that the army from the 6th of May until the 15th of June, actually, until the army -- when the JNA withdrew -- perhaps it was a few days before that. I don't know. They started this operation, the Croats and the Muslim side called this the liberation of the left bank. I don't know when this really started. But the army, with the population and with all the Serb forces, withdrew. I think that the date when I got out of Mostar, the Neretva Valley, rather because I was not in Mostar; right? I mean, at the time of the withdrawal. It was approximately the 17th of June. So it was two days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that the JNA, according to the orders they received, left Bosnia-Herzegovina and therefore Mostar as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say about this is what I saw myself, and what I heard myself, what Perisic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In addition to this peril concerning the attack on Mostar on the 6th of May, which never happened, actually, I can see here that on page 3 you say that at the beginning of 1990 the representatives of Serbs from Borovo Naselje went to meet Rade Kontic, who was the prime minister of Yugoslavia or Serbia at the time. You say that that is 1990. Well, do you know that in 1990 Ante Markovic was prime minister of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for that paragraph, could you please read it in its entirety? Because it says here quite explicitly that I heard this story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have a copy of his statement. Just a moment. Yes. What was the -- do you have the passage, Witness C-017? Or we'll get the accused to mention it again. You do. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely what I'm saying. In this voluminous statement of yours, you mainly talk about various rumours, gossip that you heard, including jokes, like the one how -- who introduced themselves to Kontic. Well, read it yourself. You say. "In the beginning of the 1990s -- 1990, Milenko, as a representative of the Serbs from Borovo Naselje, went to meet Rade Kontic, who was at the time prime minister of Yugoslavia or Serbia." He could not have been prime minister of Serbia. He comes from Montenegro; much later he was prime minister of Yugoslavia. That is correct. However, in 1990, Kontic was not prime minister. In 1990, Ante Markovic was prime minister. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said at the beginning that I'm totally apolitical. That is the first thing. And secondly, if you're reading this sentence, it says at the end, "I'm not sure." So these people are quite irrelevant to me. It was actually another person that was being referred to here, and I only talked about what had to do with him -- or rather, what I heard. As for your claims concerning rumours and things like that, I still have scars here from prison. Here I do not have my own teeth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going into that, how the HVO tortured you, kicked out your teeth, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I'm talking about the Serb prison in Trebinje, because for me there is no difference whatsoever, because there were beasts in human form on both sides, but they just wore different insignia. That's the only difference. I mean, so much for rumours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. What I said to you about Kontic, I imagine that's not being disputed. It's not difficult to establish who was prime minister when. Now, let us take this in order, please, because you devote a large part of your statement to different people. So judging by your statement, I assume that you did not put all of their names down according to significance but, rather, according to the alphabet, from A onwards. You have some 13, 14 pages of persons whose names you mention. So I'd like to take this in order, although we don't have to go through all of this. The first person you mention on page 2 - you mentioned him just now as well - in your statement, a certain Slavko Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that he was a Chetnik commander and that he committed various atrocities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you said that he held the line. The frontline you mean; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for that, the frontline, the Jewish cemetery is less than 50 metres away from Grbavica. So he was there. His men were on this line, but every shift has yet another shift coming, so they slept at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Talking about him and his men, is it in dispute, is it an issue that all these people were from Sarajevo, as you say, mostly from Grbavica and other parts of Sarajevo? I'm reading your own statement here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, yes. First and foremost, I know them in passing. I didn't have a lot of contact with them. The only person that I can really remember and who was not from Sarajevo was a certain Valera from Russia. As for the others, there were all kinds there, but most of them were from Sarajevo and the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say, and I quote you, "His unit was full of criminals from Sarajevo. It didn't have a particular name. They were known as Seselj's Chetniks from Grbavica." How come Seselj had Chetniks at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where did Slavko Aleksic get his Vojvoda title, of which he was so proud?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They seem to have distributed titles over there at will. But tell me, as you say that he killed six members of the French Foreign Legion in Sarajevo, did you see his men killing those six people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard this from Slavko Aleksic in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see, you heard it from him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from his own lips.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You know of hunters of wartime stories.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So do you believe that to be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was true, because later on - I can't remember with whom I was talking; somebody from the military police - as the legionnaires were stationed at the bridge at Vrbanja, because there was an organisation at the time that people from the Serbian side could go to the Muslim side and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But we've cleared that up. You didn't see him kill those people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard it from Slavko Aleksic himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. So that is what you say. Then you go on to say that a certain Rajo Bozovic was a close associate of Frenki Simatovic. Is it true that you didn't really know this man, that you met him in a coffee bar in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then you go on to say Dragan Bozovic, known as Giska, he was killed by Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan's men. Is it true that you know about this only on the basis of certain stories?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it says here, I learnt this from Aco Legija, so not just any stories but from him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What I meant was on the basis of what he said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You also say of him that he was one of those members of the Red Berets who were trained in Knin. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about Aco Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And you say that he was about 45 years old, thinning hair, worker's features, as you put it, and he always wore a green beret and a red one only when he reported to Frenki -- or rather, when he calls up Frenki on the telephone, he puts a red beret on his head.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's very shallow. I said this because I remember that Aco Legija always wore a green beret. As for Frenki, I was talking about the report that he -- the way he reported to Frenki, that at that time he wore a red beret.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I read out to you what you said here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To avoid any confusion, I didn't write anything. I made a statement, which was taken down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
