utterances.text: Oh, I see. Other people took it down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't write anything. I made a statement. And as has been said, during the proofing, when I came here, many details were corrected and I approved of those corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on, then. You mention a certain Gajo, a Montenegrin. You say that he was a Serb extremist, that he blew up a railway bridge in Vrapcici near Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where is this in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page 3, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Gajo Crnogorac from the day I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether you knew him. But you say that he blew up a railway bridge at Vrapcici near Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the bridge destroyed, but I didn't see him do it, but I heard it from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you saw it and you said you didn't.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bridge was at Vrapcici near Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say, with respect to some of these people that you list here a moment ago, "I mentioned they went to see Kontic," who of course was not the prime minister in 1990 or 1991 -- you say that they took part in breaking through the Croatian defences in Borovo Selo. That's what you said, and that he hit a truck full of Croatian soldiers with Zolja, a hand-held rocket launcher, and killed everyone except the person sitting next to the driver, who was wounded in the leg and this leg was later amputated. This is the one but last paragraph on page 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That doesn't matter what page it is. First of all, it's not correct that I mention Borovo Selo. I said Borovo Naselje. As regards this story, it comes directly from this man, because I worked in providing security for that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please: Did you ever inquire about the actual event in Borovo Selo and what really happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really make any inquiries, because as I have underlined, I am apolitical as far as those things are concerned, but I did hear as to what had happened in Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know what happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard of the story that the Croats entered, creating a circus, that there was shooting. I heard that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was no such incident as somebody hitting a truck with a hand-held launcher and killing everyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about the Kozaracka Street in Borovo Naselje, not Borovo Selo. I underline, Borovo Naselje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You heard all this from somebody; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says here. It is the story of the person who lost his leg. It is his story and not mine. As far as I know and as far as I was able to see - and I'm not blind - the man really doesn't have a leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But this need not have anything to do with this. Do you know that then the Croatian policeman who raided Borovo Selo was saved thanks to the intervention of a JNA unit, who made it possible for them to leave Borovo Selo and for the conflicts to quiet down that had broken out then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about two different incidents here. We started with the story about the man without a leg. I was talking about Borovo Naselje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, since obviously you listened to all those stories about what was going on over there, that groups were organised, groups of Croatian extremists to terrorise Serb populations, to carry out silent liquidations, et cetera? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mention on page 4, fourth paragraph, a certain Pasko Cibaric from Vukovar. You say that his house was used as a disco club, and that in a well in his yard a certain Seljo threw in two Croats that he had killed. Is this something that you stated on the basis of rumours and stories that you heard from others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since you are mentioning that incident, will you please read the following sentence, in the same paragraph, because it goes on to say that such and such a man told me about this incident, and he personally was working on the renovation of that house where the well is located. So it says clearly on the basis of what I made that statement, it says, "Cibaric Pasko, he's a Croat from Borovo Naselje, Trpinski Put, I believe number 31. He fled from Vukovar, and his house was later used as a disco club. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. His name, unknown, somebody called Seljo, allegedly killed two Croats and threw them in a well that was in the yard of the house. Later on they covered the well with a concrete slab. Zoran Manov told me about this incident. He was personally working on the renovation of the house and he saw where the well was located. Zoran Manov currently lives in Canada." That is all it says. So I think it is quite clear on what basis I said that. You have Zoran Manov there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is so this man Zoran Manov who is in Canada he told you he had renovated this house and he found two corpses there? Is that what he told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me exactly what is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So even he didn't mention that he saw this but that he heard that this Seljo, whose surname is unknown, threw those two Croats into the well. Now, tell me, please: You speak about Pero Divljak, who allegedly was a member of the Red Berets, and you say - and this is on page 4, paragraph 6 - that he was accused for the criminal act of drug trafficking and that allegedly Franko Simatovic saved him from prison by linking him to Mihalj Kertes, who immediately engaged him to distribute weapons in the Knin theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is Pero Divljak's story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Rather an unbelievable story.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's his story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The story of this Pero Divljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you keep mentioning him. Where is he now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the most recent information is that he is in a psychiatric institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. Is it true that at the time when these things allegedly occurred that you spoke about you didn't even know this Pero Divljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which things?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That he was connected to Kertes, Simatovic, and so on. At the time these things were happening, you didn't even know him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you're saying that he's in a mental care institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A man who's a drug addict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, he's not a drug addict, at least not in the period I knew him. But on the basis of what I saw with my own eyes and on the basis of what he told me, I'm not in the least bit surprised that he is in a mental care institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: If he's in such an institution, do you then assume that what he told you has to be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, because I saw him in action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. But you don't know, nor you ever saw Kertes, I assume?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did you ever see Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You claim you saw him with long hair, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a paragraph from a statement where it says that I went to Pule and not -- I didn't go to Pule. I went to Rijeka. When I saw him in civilian clothes, he had longer hair. But not as far as his shoulder. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say as far as his shoulder. I said long hair.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said he had longer hair. It means it wasn't cut properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. I see. You say that Miroslav Duka was a chief of police in the Serbian Autonomous Region of Herzegovina and that he and Boro Todorovic was tasked with ethnic cleansing in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [redacted]. And that is why I ended up the way I did and on the basis of statements of people from Trebinje of Muslim ethnicity that I spoke to in Niksic and all of them remember Duka and the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can we again note that you don't know personally about any of these things but that you heard it from others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. I wasn't in Trebinje at the time this was happening. I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what were they to have been tasked for any kind of operations over there? You said that he was the chief of police. And what was this other man, this Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that statement, it says nicely they saw Boro Todorovic only once, [redacted] [redacted]. And it says very nicely that I only saw them once, so that this man in a red beret who I saw then, I didn't -- I have no idea who he was. He ended up in Trebinje. How long he stayed there, what exactly he did, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Are we now in -- did we mention in open session that you feared the Red Berets when you left? We spoke about that in public session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether it was in open or closed session. I think it was in open session. I really don't know. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please explain to me: It appear that is the lady opposite is confirming that it was in open session -- explain to me, please, since in your statement later on you say that you met -- I mentioned Rajo Bozovic, I don't know who else, in a coffee bar in Belgrade later on. When was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the period roughly in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now, if they were the Red Berets and you were terribly afraid of them, thinking that they might kill you, how did you dare then go and meet with them, talk to them, when you were afraid of them killing you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding Rajo Bozovic himself, I pointed out very clearly that a man showed me Rajo Bozovic. Until then, I had never seen him, nor did he see me. As for my movements --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see him either, but somebody pointed him out to you and said, "That is Rajo Bozovic"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is what it says in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. I just want to establish that. You didn't meet him personally; somebody pointed him out to you and said, "That is that man"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you were in Belgrade. You had contact with those people, the people you feared.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't contact them. I had no contact with them at all. I was there. That means, as far as the Red Berets are concerned, the only man I contacted was Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dragan Vasiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But somewhere in your statement - and I'm sure you'll remember - you said that I wrote him a letter of some kind. How can you say something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't claim that you wrote a letter to him. I saw a piece of paper with your signature on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: With my signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with your signature. And it was an order that was sent to General Perisic, and the unit, I think it's name was Suncokreti, sun flower, at the 4th of July barracks should be disbanded urgently because members of that unit, Captain Dragan's men, were from the camp in Fruska, people from Serbian Krajina --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you. My position with regard to the paramilitaries has been common knowledge for the past ten years. I consider that they should all be disbanded. But there was no letter or order to General Perisic in this connection. You couldn't have seen something like that, because quite simply it did not exist.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this with my own eyes from Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. So then I suppose the document would have to exist in the general staff, if it existed at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ask Vasiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't need to ask him. Quite simply, it's not true. Now, let's move on. Although my position was always that the paramilitaries couldn't be tolerated - this was a common stance of mine, well known to everyone; it was no secret - but you mention - and tell me this now, please - a certain man called Duka, Sinisa, in fact, Duka Sinisa, who allegedly exhumed bodies that had been killed by the Red Berets. That's what you say. Now, is it true that you never actually saw anything like that, you never saw him exhuming bodies of any kind, nor that these were the bodies of people killed by members of the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When those people were killed, that means the very act of killing them, killing these innocent civilians, people who were born in the same place I was born in, I saw that. Sinisa Duka is just like me. He's a Serb who ended up in a Croatian and Muslim prison. The name of the prison was Celovina. And those volunteers, as they liked to call themselves very proudly at that, did this. What they did was that if anybody had a chance of surviving in the prison, they were beaten to death. Because of those killed civilians -- now, I grew up in the same area as Sinisa Duka, and I saw -- I didn't see him actually exhume bodies. I wasn't able to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That was my only question to you. That's all I asked you. You didn't see that either. Now, second point: Tell me, please, because nobody in Mostar knows of any kind of mass killing of people which you allegedly saw take place on the embankment, on the river bank of the Neretva River --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly, this term of yours, allegedly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Go on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This term "allegedly" has no place here, because it was more than 100 people. So allegedly" is quite out of order. That's provocation. There's something that cannot be wiped out, and those are the grave, graves that I visited in 1998. And I saw the names and surnames of people whom I knew from those parts. So this "alleged," the term "alleged" that you use, is completely out of place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you saw the graves of some people in 1998, did you? I'm not asking you about that. I'm not asking whether you saw graves in 1998. What I'm claiming is that you could not have seen any killings going on in 1992, the ones that you said you saw and watched from the roof of some house and that you were watching and saw this man Divljak -- is Divljak his nickname, I assume?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That you saw him slaughter some people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as this fact goes, not to enter into a debate on that point, there's a problem if you wish to prove the opposite. There's a man, he's a man now; he was a child then -- who survived the massacre. And it will be a little difficult for you to prove that nothing actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just explain to you. It is not up to me to prove anything here. It is up to you to prove that what you're saying is the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. The massacre existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How come nobody knows about it in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. The whole of Mostar knows about it, and it is precisely because of those volunteer units that the Serbs of Mostar that have nothing to do with anything. They were normal people who spent their entire life working from that time on and people who have returned have -- are facing very great problems precisely because of that event, because that is something that the Muslims cannot forget. And I completely understand them on that score.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Of course crimes can't be forgotten. If one man is killed, that is a major event. And you say you saw many more of them killed and you say that ten, in fact, in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said you saw 500 killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say 500.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Just wait a moment. You must pause. Remember the interpreters who have to keep up. If you would both remember that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never mentioned the figure of 500. You're trying to put that in many mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday, that's what you said, that there were 500 of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was this, and I said it exactly and precisely as we're playing around with words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not playing around with words. I've noted what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. I said yesterday that had I -- that I knew at least 500 people from that settlement. That's what I said, I knew at least 500 people from those parts. And the context in which I said this was as follows: I said I couldn't see the faces. I couldn't see the face of the victim and say, "This is Osman or this is Ibro." But in that context, I said that some of the people amongst the people whom I knew were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's not waste time on that. So you said the 500, you mentioned the 500 in a different context, and you said you saw him kill ten; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you counted this. And these killings were perpetrated by Divljak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count them. I said at least ten. But as I wasn't watching Pero Divljak alone -- he wasn't alone there. So he wasn't the only one I watched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I understood it that you were with him all the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're trying to put words into my mouth again. I wasn't with him. You have it precisely described in my statement, where I was, the course I traversed, and why I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Very well. That's just fine. Now, you mention a certain man called Dusan Durutovic, nicknamed Duco, and then another man called Tosa, and you don't know his proper name, but you say that they were instructors in the centre for training at Tara. Did you see these men at Tara, at Mount Tara, the people working as instructors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them up at Mount Tara. The police uniform and US-manufactured uniforms with red berets -- Dusan Durutovic, yes, I did see him wearing that. Or let me apologise. I mean with the brown wolf as the insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So these Brown Wolves, who are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw that insignia for the first time at the camp at Buna worn by the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The Brown Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So how did you link them up to the police of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not up to me to link them up. What I said was that they were wearing the police uniform of Dusan Durutovic. I saw his uniform, and the US-manufactured uniform, I did see that. I saw it in his -- on his premises, behind the discotheque that he was rented out. I think that the discotheque's name was Leonardo, but I can't remember. It was in Samobor, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, you mentioned Captain Dragan a moment ago -- this is on page 10, last paragraph -- and you say you saw him in a cafe in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How did you get to know him at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't want to meet him. That's the first point. Secondly, the man who is the proprietor of the cafe is part proprietor with a man they call Doc. I don't know what his real name is. But he was a sort of doctor. And he was a member of Captain Dragan's units. And that's how he comes to know Captain Dragan, and that's why Captain Dragan frequented his cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. You said you talked to Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you claim you talked to Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, when you cite the statement, could you just indicate the paragraph number handwritten on the left side. Do you have that kind of statement? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well, Mr. Kwon. What I was asking him is on -- on page 10, last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That's paragraph 69. We found it. But we would be assisted if you indicate the number, the paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 6, paragraphs 1 and 2 this time, you speak about the people who were in command of the camp, the Red Berets, a man named Pajzos -- a place called Pajzos. Have you ever been to Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to Bapska, but not the Pajzos camp itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you weren't actually there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me of any operation, any action undertaken by the people in the camp that you were not in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that -- what that's got to do with my statement. Because in my statement, I spoke about an operation undertaken by the Red Berets in the place I was at, so I don't know what Pajzos has got to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know either. That's why I'm asking myself, why do you have in your statement something that has nothing to do with you. You say you weren't there, and yet you speak about people in a camp and a base of some kind of these forces where you never were. Now, you're talk about their activities. So what's that got to do with your statement? That's my question to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked about the camps I knew about and how I came to know about the camps. Now, as to the activities of these people from Pajzos, Zvjezdan Jovanovic, case in point, I know that from another man who was from Ilok, and he was an instructor from the Red Berets from the very beginning. His name was Ilija Vuckovic, nicknamed Rambo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So these different pieces of information you managed to collect from this Ilija Vuckovic, Rambo, person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that's what you talk about in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it wasn't on the basis of your own experience or you as an eyewitness but on the basis of what other people told you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I did my best to underline what was my own personal experience and what I had heard from others. So when they asked me, I explained this in great detail. I said what happened and what I had seen take place, if I was present, and also I said what I had heard from others. I was very careful to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But you mention various people throughout your statement. I would have to quote a lot of places. You mention Krajisnik. You've mentioned Martic. You've mentioned Simatovic. Seselj, Maras, Perisic, Ante Roso, Captain Dragan, a host of people here and so on and so forth. And then you tell us what you think about those people. So what has that got to do with anything? What does it matter what you think about Ante Roso, Perisic, Martic, or anyone else? What are you actually saying? What are you stating? Explain that to me, please. I can't understand what you're on about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why you're treating me like somebody working in the Tribunal. I was asked. They asked me what happened and what I know about these events, and I stated that loud and clear. I answered their question very clearly. So it's a simple matter. The people I knew about and whom I saw doing what they did, that's what I said. As to the things I heard about, I underlined this and said I heard about them and we don't have to go into that any more. But I don't know if you know; I don't work for the Tribunal. I don't write the statements. I'm just a witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That's a very good answer. Excellent. Now, you go on to say on page 6, the penultimate paragraph --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, page 6, one but last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mention a certain man called Tomo Kovac, the Minister of the interior of Republika Srpska. I know the name and I know he was the Minister of the Interior, Tomo Kovac. Now, you say you saw an order which in April 1992 was signed by him, an order of some kind --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That called for criminals to be put under RS MUP control, the control of the MUP of Republika Srpska. And you say you saw the document in the Sarajevo -- in Sarajevo in Kula.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document that you've just mentioned, I did see in the police station at Kula, and the chief of the police station was, very interestingly, Goran Sehovac, Cena. He was an assistant to the baker.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's not go into the fact of who was a deputy in the police station in Sarajevo. Tell me this, please: What does this mean, that criminals should be placed under the control of the RS MUP? I assume that it is the role of the minister to place criminals under somebody's control, under the control of the police. I assume that that is his task.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a normal state. But down there, it was just one unit that had looted anything it came across. So it was a unit led by a man whose name was Pinjo [phoen]. And I heard about him in Mostar even before the war, because he was such a major criminal, this Pinjo, generally known, and that's why I underlined that the head of the police station was in fact a baker who's in prison now. So you can see what Tomo Kovac had in mind when he wrote this down and said they should be placed in control of the MUP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I understand it from all this, he intervened precisely because of the criminal offences that these people were carrying out, and that's his job, as chief of police. It's his job to intervene if criminals are engaged in criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First of all, Tomo Kovac, I know him personally, you see, so it's not that I'm -- I haven't heard of him; I know him personally and I can tell you that. He cannot react against criminals because Tomo Kovac is a major criminal himself. And secondly, this unit, when he said that they should be placed under the control of these men, these men were in the MUP unit commanded by this Goran Sehovac, Cena.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The one who was a baker?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a baker. He was a deputy baker, even lower down on the rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, page 7, paragraph 5 you mention a man called Ranko. His name was -- his surname was Maglov. Ranko Maglov. And you say he was a commander of the camp in Bruska in Knin. Did you ever go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, how do you know this, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember who I talked to. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know how you came by that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just can't remember. They asked me what I knew about Bruska and that was my answer. It was in the Bruska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they asked you a question. They say: What do you know about such and such a man? And you tell them what you heard from somebody else and that's all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When the statement was compiled - and I can see that you're very skilled in bypassing what I actually saw and want to base your questions on what I heard - what I said was - and I'm going to tell you this for the last time - I'm going to tell you what I saw and where I was, where I was present. So when they asked me what I heard about, if I said I heard something, then I underlined this. I stressed that I had heard it. So I really don't think there's any need for me to tell you that for the fifteenth time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what you heard about, it makes up 90 per cent of your statement. And I'm asking you because you say you allegedly say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is a pointless exchange. We've heard the point over and over again, and there's no need to go on about it. Now, have you got any more substantial questions arising from this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I do, Mr. May. As far as I can see, this witness testified for about three and a half hours in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. No. It was two and three-quarters, and you will have the same.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May. Your arithmetic and mine often do not coincide. But let me go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say on page 8 that a certain Milosevic whose name you don't know but you only know his nickname, Boco, was in direct contact with Simatovic and said that he was coming to Belgrade in order to get weapons and equipment that was needed in Bosnia. Were you ever present during any such contact between this Boco and Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not between them personally. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How do you have this kind of information, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a bit slippery, but you got this wrong. I've known Boco since I was born, but I don't know his name until the present day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I will not go into all of that. I'm asking you about what you know about his connection with Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what he said to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, what he said to you. Let's go on, then. Then also you say Ribic Nikola, nicknamed Kanada, was he an emigre who had come from Canada?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's no emigre. He came for a safari, to hunt people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He came from Canada?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he lived in Canada?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he came from Canada straight to Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And where did he fight? In which unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found him in the White Wolves unit. I don't know where he was before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The White Wolves were a unit of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you say that they were under the direct control of Ratko Mladic, not the commander of the Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that also has nothing to do with Serbia or any forces from Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand this question. You asked me about Ribic. You asked me who he was. And I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to establish that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was also highlighted in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that a certain Vuckovic, Ilija, was a member of the DB, and that he was in charge of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, from him. Very well. All right. On page 11, in the one but last paragraph, you give information about some men. You talk about Crni, Danijel, Boco, Goran, and you don't know what their names are. Is that right? Or do you perhaps know their names? Can you identify them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me about Boco, Crni. I know these people. I saw Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Crni. I never asked him what his name was because I wasn't interested. An absolutely irrelevant person in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to make any assumptions to that effect, as to whether they were important in your life or not. I just want to ask you about your testimony, what you know about these men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crni, I know, was commander of the unit that called itself Vukovarci. They had come with Novica Gusic. I know about Crni, that he was one of the main people involved in the ethnic cleansing of Nevesinje, cleansing of the Muslim population. And Crni, I know he took part in the action in Podvelezje. And that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. While we're still on the subject of Mostar, since you say that you were not interested in politics and since you are a Yugoslav by ethnicity, you do not distinguish between people on the basis of ethnic backgrounds, but there were clashes there between predominantly Serb, predominantly Croat, and predominantly Muslim forces; is that right? You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So do you know about these events from 1991 to 1995, how many Serbs were killed in the area of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period from 1991 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that period when various clashes started, various killings, 1991 to 1995. In 1995, the war was over.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that as for the killing of civilians or abuse of civilians, I made a statement about that. I can say that while I was down there in prison, there were quite a few civilians there of Serb ethnicity, in the prison that was held by the Croat Muslim forces. As for killings in the surrounding area in the villages, mountains, et cetera, I really know nothing about that. I've already said -- I pointed out that I absolutely was not interested. Had I been interested, I would have gotten out of Mostar, because I did not believe that any such thing could happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody believed it. [redacted] there were very close relations in Mostar for decades, especially between Serbs and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina, their research centre for investigating crimes committed against the Serb people, and it pertains to Mostar only --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen, if you are interested in the truth, I don't know whether you will express any interest in this report at all, but half of this report are lists of persons who actually perpetrated the crimes. I cannot read it, but I'm going to read it to you. I'm going to give you the first name. I won't go any further. Again, they started from A.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I suggest we go into private session, because we have observed now that even when Mr. Milosevic poses the question quite in a neutral way, the answer is very specific and related to the witness as such and his being in a certain place and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's see how we get on. Yes. Ask the question. We'll see how we get.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None of this can identify the witness. I'm reading out of a book of reports. I'm reading the first and -- I can give the second and third names if you wish as well. Abaz Dervo, from Mostar, place of birth, Sarica. Date and place of crime, 7th of April, 1992 in Mostar. Participant in the liquidation of 19 Serbs who were tied up and taken out of Mostar to Herzegovina. They were then killed and thrown into a pit." Then after him, yet another participant. A few of them did this. It wasn't only one man. So it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with these one at a time. One at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any knowledge about these crimes? I can give you this book as a present, [redacted]. Half of the book is a report about the criminals who committed these crimes. And since you deal with volunteers, there's even a chapter about volunteers here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer these points. Now, you are being asked about a crime, when it's alleged that on the 7th of April, 1992, it said there was a liquidation of 19 Serbs who were thrown into a pit. Now, do you know anything about any such event? Have you any information as to whether there was such an event or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already pointed out that if we're talking about the beginning of April, that I was in prison. So not even theoretically could I have known about any such thing while I was in prison. As for the book itself, I read it a long time ago, and I know what this is all about. The crime itself that you referred to, I think it took place on the 7th of April. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already presented the reason why I cannot be aware of this. I heard about it, and I -- what I know -- I mean -- I know a lot of Serbs. I have Croat friends, Muslim friends, and I have Serb friends as well,

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] A lot of people did not manage to get out. And I have already said why I personally cannot know about what happened on the 7th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Witness. I hope that you understood me. I gave you the name of the first person on this list of criminals just to give me some information if you know anything about this. But half of the book are perpetrators of these crimes. It's not really a book. It's a report with names. And you say that you saw this. In addition to the introduction where the dates are specified as to what happened when, the next chapter that starts with a list is called "Victims," victims. The total number is 502, 502 Serbs were killed in Mostar at the time. Did you perhaps see any of their graves? Did you establish how any of them were killed? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I know that quite a few Serbs were killed down there, [redacted],

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about mass graves. I'm asking you whether you know anything about these 502 Serb victims in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably do, because there have to be people among them who I had known personally.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen, if you are interested in the truth, the truth that is quite contrary to this impression that you've gained on the basis of this testimony, I will give it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't make a speech. At the moment you haven't yet produced that. The witness, to produce it, you can call in evidence in due course, if that's what you want. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mention on page 13 a certain Major Fico, or a certain Marko from -- Marko Sasovac and you claim that they had trained the Red Berets. Is it correct that you actually never saw these people, actually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Major Fico on a cassette, as I said there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, on a cassette. But I asked: Is it true that you never saw any one of them in person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that they do not originally come from Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, you mean they are not from Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You're sure about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I have to ask the witness -- actually, I have to put some questions to him that have to do with questions that Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff put to him in private session at the very beginning, and they have to do with him personally, so I don't want to jeopardise his identity in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But could you please be as brief as possible in your answers so this private session would not go on for too long.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I interrupt, just to -- before the accused resumes his cross-examination to explain what our position is on timetable for the week. It might help the accused and I can't be here at 2.00. If this witness finishes today, we will hope to deal with tomorrow's witness, Mr. Selak, in one day. If we can deal with him sufficiently briefly in chief, which I hope we can. We would still hope to finish the two other witnesses scheduled for this week on Friday. I hope that's possible. I can best achieve that - and this is why I want the accused to know this in advance - by taking the expert, Dr. Babovic, very briefly, as is allowed for in the rules and doing little more than simply submitting his report with a few supplementary questions. And were it possible for him to be concluded in the first two sessions on Friday and were the application for 92 bis for B-1047, which has been heralded in advance and will be formally before you soon, were that to be granted, we would hope to conclude him in the third session. We realise there has been a little overrun of the witnesses this week, but we are anxious because of forthcoming time-tabled witnesses we are anxious to finish it this week if possible. Obviously if there were any additional time available to us, we would be grateful. But that is my present time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you will have until 2.00, which is perhaps some 15 or 20 minutes more. There's a matter I'd like to raise with you. You often refer to Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff as the lady opposite. That's a discourtesy which is gratuitous and it does your cause no good. It doesn't become you. She calls you by your name, Mr. Milosevic, or the accused. You should show her the same respect. I should also say it's a discourtesy to the Chamber, because she's an officer of the Court. Continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I very frequently use the name of Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff. However, it sometimes happens that I forget her name and that is when I use that expression. It is quite true that it is below one's dignity to be insulting and discourteous. That is not at all my intention, regardless of what opinion I have of everyone's role here, of all those present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No explanation needed. Continue your cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to explain to me what Mr. Nice said a moment ago? That is, the registrar told me that there would be no changes this week in the order of witnesses. This witness is due to complete his testimony today. Tomorrow we have Mr. Selak planned. And he mentioned several witnesses for Friday. According to my list, there are another two witnesses, no expert witnesses. I don't see when all these can fit into the time available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's not take up any more time about it. The order follows that which you already have. The expert who's referred to is a Dr. Babovic, who's an expert on the police.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. I have only two more questions regarding this witness personally, so I wish that to be clear.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, since you lived there, that as early as the end of the '80s, in 1989 and even in 1988, in Western Herzegovina when people were going to the army Ustasha songs were sung and songs in favour of Ante Pavelic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't see what that has to do with my statement. But let me try and explain with respect to that. When I say that I come from there, it means that the people from the hills, that we call Brdjani, people in Western Herzegovina and Eastern Herzegovina, what you are saying is quite true, but also Chetnik songs were sung in Nevesinje, not in 1988 but in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted you to tell me whether what I am saying is true. Now, tell me: Is it true that when the HDZ appeared on the scene - you know that is the Croatian Democratic Union - the explanation of Herzegovina was that it was an all-national organisation called the Herzegovina Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have absolutely no knowledge about that. Because I've already explained I'm an absolutely apolitical person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that many people who were not members of the Croatian National Union, in April 1992 had problems with members of the Croatian Armed Forces, the so-called HOS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that on the basis of my own example, personal example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you do have some knowledge on the basis of your personal experience and I assume on the basis of the experience of others as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And are you aware of examples of members of the HOS going to people's apartments, of those people who did not belong to the HDZ, informing them that all Serbs have to leave Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please: Had you heard or do you have any knowledge about it that in April and May 1992 several private improvised camps were established, such as the JNA ambulance? These were established by the HOS. Then the basement of the economics and law faculty in the Aleksa Santic Elementary School, and two legal state prisons, HVO, in Celovina and a HOS prison at the military clinic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are saying about the military clinic and Celovina, that is one in the same thing. That prison was a private prison of Mensur Cumic. Whether he was linked to HOS or not, I don't know, because I didn't see that man in my course of stay in Mostar. I explained the reasons for this. I had heard about it. As regards prisons, there were prisons on both sides, just as the prison in Bileca was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But I'm now asking you about this one. So is it true what I'm saying about these private and what I would call official prisons, penitentiary -- penitentiaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said which prison I was in, and I had indeed heard about those prisons that you mention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know at least how many -- at all how many prisons and camps there were in which Serbs were detained in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. You don't know anything about that. You spoke about a camp -- or rather, a base of the various units at Buna; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you were shown here the patch of the Serbian Chetnik Movement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My understanding was that you explained that you saw that patch -- I don't mean you personally, but any, any of the citizens who may have been interested could have bought such a patch in the street. It was in circulation as a kind of label or sticker.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you mentioned the White Eagles, do you know that they have nothing to do with Seselj or the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in that camp, were there various volunteers from various parts of the former SFRY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have explained and as I said in my statement, the first time I explained how I got there and what I found in that camp. I said, and I'm saying again, that it was a group of criminals collected from here, there, and everywhere, wearing all kinds of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You're speaking -- you mention a so-called Boro Todorovic on page 18, paragraph 5, and you say that he was the commander of the operative group 1 of the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We have established -- we had established earlier on where they are from, and saying that there was a total of some ten of them. What kind of operative or operational group 1 are you talking about? Is that the group that you spoke about, or is this something else that you talk about here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I said with precision that I saw Boro Todorovic once on that occasion when I arrived. Boro Todorovic had with him another group, and I don't talk about that group. The group I'm referring to in my statement is the group that stayed at the Boracko Jezero. Boro Todorovic's group, who they were, I have no idea, because that same day they left with the police that had escorted me there. They left to go to Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since on page 19 in the last paragraph you say that you were a member of the Red Berets of the Bosnian branch; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that I was a member of the Red Berets. I was picked up by force to be a guide. That is how it started.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just check something, because I'm not quite sure about it. My emphasis is on the Bosnian branch. Do you know that the Red Berets of Serbia did not even exist at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any Red Beret members from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those I listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Didn't you say that they were people trained by Captain Dragan at the Knin fortress and that they had come from Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is Krajina the same as Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not, but it wasn't Dragan Simantic [phoen], but Franko Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Simatovic who was also in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Franko Simatovic headed the intelligence administration of the state security service. He didn't engage in what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. But if he was engaging in those activities, the journalists of Express Politika in Knin and he was that at the same time, these two don't go together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: People engaging in intelligence can do all kinds of things, as you know very well. You speak about the Eagles and other paramilitary formations. Is it true that General Momcilo Perisic was very angry because of the presence of those paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the position of the army was that volunteers can only join the JNA and the Territorial Defence and place themselves under their command, that it would not tolerate paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that, and I explained why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In your statement, on page 18, you mentioned the so-called punitive platoon, belonging to the Red Berets and under the command of a certain Zivojin Ivanovic. Were you a member of that platoon, that you have that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. But Pero Divljak, whose -- whom Zika Crnogorac is and Profa [phoen], Dule Bokser, Samir Catic, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. As far as I could see from your statement, you base all your information on what you heard from this Divljak; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right. Not all information. Because you have been asking me here all the time about what I had heard, and that's what I've been answering you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that this man, Zivojin Ivanovic, Zika Crnogorac, was not in Herzegovina at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Podvelezje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did you see him in Podvelezje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said at the very outset that it was sometime in July approximately, the same day when I escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does this man look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What he looks like?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what can I say about Zika? He's quite tall. He has a very crooked nose. And I had a few close encounters with Zika.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so he's a very tall man. All right. You talk about the plunder of some neighbourhoods in Mostar by reservists, and then you mentioned the White Eagles and you even mention policemen. I assume because you're from the area that you knew these policemen personally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the policemen themselves, now that we're talking about them, who were under Duka's command, I did know some of them from the area but there were policemen there from Bileca, Nevesinje, Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But all that is the same region, Mostar, Trebinje, Nevesinje, Bileca. I mean, all of this is within 50 kilometres, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But never in my life before that was I in Nevesinje, Gacko, or Trebinje, because -- I mean, this part of Herzegovina was simply quite irrelevant, as far as I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any possibility whatsoever to personally see some of the looting that they were carrying out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You mean policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for policemen -- as for policemen, I have nothing to say really, except to ask them what cars did they drive at the time in 1992, with civilian license plates from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this for another reason, since you knew these people, you saw them, you knew them, you established that they were policemen from the area, that they were looting. So practically you did not have the opportunity of reporting them to anyone, because you'd have to report them to themselves.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have nothing to report to anyone, because everybody who was there - everybody - all these units that I mentioned, were involved in plundering, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. When you say "all of them" --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- So you're only excluding yourself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not only myself. There were other young men there too, who really didn't take a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So not everybody was involved in plundering. You weren't, and there were some others who weren't involved in it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were others too, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's clarify that too. You mentioned that somebody who was close to me --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- together with some other men at the proposal of an Albanian who was doing his military service killed a Croat in the streets of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the killing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you in a position then, at least, to approach any members of the military and to report that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. I, as an individual who is absolutely meaningless there and whose life is in jeopardy, I'm supposed to report that and the captains, the security officers who were there, I mean the regular JNA, Captain Rade Mihajlovic, officially, if he has nothing to report, what have I got to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that this Captain Rade Mihajlovic saw that too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You saw that too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, please: You say on page 22 that there was a lot of fighting around the bridge in Lucko. Is it correct that on the other hand, there was some kind of a Muslim fortification, sandbags, machine-guns, things like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were sealed off for two hours there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what happened then? Did you withdraw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for that, this was the second day of the attack, because the first night we came to a place which is called Mali Mejdan. On the other side, the members of the 63rd Airborne Brigade were stuck by Lucki Most, and the same night they were bombed from the hill of Hum by artillery. So they didn't manage to destroy the bridge, it didn't fall all together, but it was half-damaged. It's true that we were sealed off for about two hours. After that, after a lot of gunfire, a tank got out from the Lucko bridge on the side where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, since you talk about a meeting between Captain Zoran Pejanovic, Mirko Simic, president of the Serb Democratic Party of Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was present when Pejanovic was making a speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you were not present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How can you testify about the meeting, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not testify about the meeting. I testified about Pejanovic's speech addressed to Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, about Pejanovic's speech. That's what you're testifying about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Is it correct that in the fighting around Bijelo Polje you were ambushed by the Croats when you entered the yard of the military technical institute?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They surrounded you and opened fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you actively take part in this fighting around Bijelo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the first time I used a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that the White Eagles, the local Chetniks, raped and killed nuns and civilians at the Catholic monastery in Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is quite clearly stated in my statement that that is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, all right. You did not see it yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that knowledge is also based on hearsay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That knowledge comes from the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it was precisely in mid-April 1992, in the area of the municipality of Mostar, that bridges in Grabovica on Neretvi on the road between Mostar, Sarajevo and Rotimlja, on the road between Capljina and Stolac were either destroyed or damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I explained why I could not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know about the bombing of the village and monastery of Zitomislici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the period when the JNA was withdrawing, the 15th of June, yes -- then the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So who did the bombing and who destroyed the village and the monastery of Zitomislici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know towards the end of April 1992 that the units from Zadar, Sibenik, and Imotski, belonging to HOS arrived at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that they arrived. As for the Croatian units, I can only talk about the 114th Split Brigade of Lora, that it was there at the time when we were withdrawing from the Neretva River Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know about the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And do you know about the 29th and 30th of April, when the members of HOS engaged artillery, mortar artillery and gunfire against military facilities, the airport, the northern camp, southern camp, the JNA centre, when Major Branislav Jovanovic was killed and several soldiers were seriously wounded? Do you remember that event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what was the date mentioned in your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The 29th and 30th of April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time I was either in prison down there or in prison on the Serb side. But at any rate ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know that they approached the JNA centre and that they controlled all roads leading to the JNA centre, the members of the HOS did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the JNA centre itself, I did hear that they were taken prisoner but these same soldiers were released after Perisic threatened that Western Herzegovina would be bombed. That's the only story I know, as far as the JNA centre itself is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Have you heard of mass breakings into Serbian apartments and various people illegally moving into these apartments, people who came predominantly from Western Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about arrests of ethnic Serbs in April and that they were taken to Grude and other villages in Western Herzegovina where they were exposed to mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for that period, I've already said that I myself was arrested at the time. There were prisons, yes. As for having people taken to Western Herzegovina, I can say that the people who saved me did so because they heard that they would be transported from Celovina to Dretelj. So I did hear about these transports, but it's not that I personally know of anybody being transported there had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you did hear that after this torture in Mostar prisons many Serbs were transferred to other camps, like this Dretelj, the one that you've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything -- this is a former warehouse in Capljina, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I already mentioned that Eastern and Western Herzegovina, before the war, was not a place where I went at all. Dretelj is in Western Herzegovina. The only thing I know about it is that it was used as a concentration camp for Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the conditions there and about the treatment of people who were detained at Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what I heard from people who got out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just say briefly what you heard from them, from the people who got out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are terrible things, as regards the conditions and mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many of them managed to get out, out of the total number who were detained there, and how many of them forever stayed behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, but the majority stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That is to say, they were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You have to know about this, because it happened on the 9th of May, when the village of Pribiloici was victimised and other villages, Vrapcici, Lokve, Hodbina, Blagaj, Potoci, Prigradjani, were also attacked.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. The date cannot be correct, because all Serb villages that are around Mostar were attacked on the moment -- at the moment when the JNA was withdrawing. Before that, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. When the JNA was withdrawing, all the Serb villages were attacked.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What happened to these villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including Mostar, the left bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Is this information that I have correct, namely that then all these villages were looted and destroyed and many of the local villagers were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The villages were destroyed and looted; that is correct. It is also correct that people were killed. But how many, that is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of the attack of the HVO on Goranci and Bogodol, Serb villages when all the men were killed or taken into prison in Santiceva Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogodol is a village which is on the road to Western Herzegovina. So it was always, if we can put it this way, it was always part of their territory. And I did hear about all the inhabitants of that village. That they were brought into custody in Mostar. But my information was that they were incarcerated at the mechanical faculty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In prison.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
